identification: Hand-coloured steel engraved map 'Victoria, or Port Phillip' from John Tallis & Co.'s Illustrated Atlas (drawn and engraved by J. Rapkin, vignettes after H. Warren), London c1851-53, with vignettes of a kangaroo, Aboriginal figures (two groups), a view of Melbourne/Port Phillip shipping at top, and a waterfall scene lower right, decorative scroll border. Outline/county colouring. Window mounted on a teal mount with a gold slip, in a period-style birdseye maple moulded frame (about 60 x 50 cm overall by eye). On the back, a Lahaina Printsellers Ltd (Maui, Hawaii) certificate of authenticity: subject 'Victoria or Port Phillip', publisher John Tallis, circa 1851, image 10 x 14 in, mat 18 x 22 in, 'original steelplate engraving'. Looks a genuine atlas plate. Edition (early state without the Gold Diggings marking, or later with Gold Diggings coloured and the seal lower right) cannot be read from these photos.

viewing_check: Check whether this is the early state (no Gold Diggings) or the later state with gold fields coloured yellow and a seal at lower right; read the imprint line under the border (Tallis & Co London/New York). Look for a plate mark, toning, foxing and mount burn; check the hand colour is watercolour, not printed dots (loupe). Check the frame is real birdseye maple veneer and sound, and whether the back is sealed (COA is on the backing).
